legend.soi_protection: Y = statewide source-of-income protection (voucher refusal illegal), N = none statewide, P = state PREEMPTS localities from adding one, L = local ordinances only (see quirks/note)
legend.pm_license: B = real-estate broker license required for third-party management, PM = dedicated property-management license, N = no license required (see note)
legend.eviction_speed_tier: 1 = fastest (~2-4 weeks), 2 = moderate (~1-2 months), 3 = slow (~2-4 months), 4 = slowest (4+ months, tenant-protective courts)
legend.verify_flag: true = rule changed recently or has known ambiguity - verify the controlling statute before acting on it
legend.notice.nonpay_days: statutory pay-or-quit notice before filing; string values are special regimes (e.g. 'demand', 'none - file directly')
legend.rates: annually-published figures the formulas need. value=null means the current-cycle figure is NOT loaded: output the formula + citation and say 'current-year rate not loaded' - NEVER estimate a percentage or dollar maximum. Populate values via jurisdiction_notes config rows (param 'rates.<id>.value') on each publisher's cycle.
legend.pending_change: a dated rule change: {field, new_value, effective_from, precision, citation}. Lookup applies the value in force TODAY and flags the transition; precision='year' means the exact in-year date is unverified - treat the tenant-protective side as in force and flag.
legend.return_deadline_unit: day-count type for deposit return deadlines: calendar (default) or business. When absent, count the LONGER interpretation.

cares_act_nonpay_notice_days.note: Applies to 'covered properties' (federally backed mortgage or federal housing program). The 30-day notice requirement has no statutory sunset and courts are split - safest practice is a 30-day nonpayment notice on any covered property, regardless of shorter state timelines.

fair_housing_protected_classes.citation: Fair Housing Act, 42 U.S.C. §3601 et seq.
fair_housing_protected_classes.note: Disparate-impact liability applies (HUD rule; Inclusive Communities, 2015) - a facially neutral policy that disproportionately excludes a protected class can violate the FHA. Blanket criminal-history bans risk violation under HUD's 2016 guidance (Keating memo): use individualized assessment of nature, severity, and recency.

assistance_animals.value: no pet fees, pet deposits, or pet rent for assistance animals; breed/weight restrictions do not apply
assistance_animals.note: Assistance animals (service + emotional support) are a disability accommodation, not pets. Documentation requests are limited when the disability or need is not apparent.

lead_disclosure.value: pre-1978 housing requires lead-based paint disclosure + EPA pamphlet before lease signing

scra_protections.value: eviction of active-duty servicemembers or dependents requires a court order when rent is at or below the SCRA threshold (~$10k/mo, adjusted annually); courts may stay proceedings; military-status affidavit required for default judgments

fcra_adverse_action.value: denying, conditioning, or pricing tenancy based on a consumer report (credit or tenant screening) requires an adverse-action notice naming the reporting agency

fdcpa.value: third-party collection of rent debt (including by managers collecting for owners in some circuits) is subject to FDCPA notice, validation, and conduct rules

nspire.value: HUD-assisted units are inspected under NSPIRE standards (replaced HQS/UPCS)

vawa.value: in covered federal programs, being a victim of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking cannot be the basis for denial, eviction, or termination of assistance

scra_eviction_rent_threshold.formula: DoD annual housing-cost adjustment (~monthly rent threshold below which eviction of a covered servicemember requires a court order)

hud_fmr.scope: reference via the live fmr_for_zip lookup - never cached here

deposit.penalty: failure to return on time forfeits the landlord's claim and can double recovery
deposit.note: cap excludes pet deposits and increased-risk deposits
cap applies only when rent ≤ $2,000/mo; return is 14 days when no deductions are taken, 30 days with deductions
14 business days

late_fee.rule: must be reasonable and stated in the lease

AR.name: Arkansas
quirks: Only state with NO implied warranty of habitability - landlord repair duties are largely contractual

CA.name: California

deposit.note: small landlords (≤2 properties, ≤4 units, natural person) may take 2 months; some local ordinances require interest

late_fee.rule: enforceable only as a valid liquidated-damages provision

notice.mtm_termination_days: 30 (<1 yr) / 60 (≥1 yr); just cause required after 12 months (AB 1482)

quirks: AB 1482 statewide rent cap: 5% + CPI, max 10%, for covered buildings 15+ years old
Dense local overlays (LA, SF, Oakland, San José, etc.) with stricter rent control and just-cause rules than state law
CA.overlay_note: Never answer from state law alone - check the city ordinance

ab1482_max_increase.formula: 5% + regional CPI, capped at 10%; applies to the Aug 1 - Jul 31 window
ab1482_max_increase.publisher: CA DOJ / CAA tables, annually (April CPI)

local_board_increases.formula: board-specific: SF 60% of CPI, Berkeley 65% of CPI; Oakland, Santa Monica, and LA RSO each set annually
local_board_increases.scope: local rent-control boards - always check the board, never AB 1482 alone

application_screening_fee_cap.formula: statutory base adjusted annually by CPI

CO.name: Colorado

deposit.note: cap was 2 months under SB23-184; a 1-month cap takes effect in 2026 - the lookup applies the value in force today and flags the change; lease may extend return to 60 days

pending_change.citation: SB23-184 follow-on; verify the exact effective date and any small-landlord carve-outs

late_fee.rule: greater of $50 or 5% of overdue amount

quirks: No-cause terminations are banned (HB24-1098) - every non-renewal needs an enumerated cause
CO.overlay_note: Denver and Boulder require rental licenses to operate

deposit.note: cap is 1 month for tenants 62+; deadline is 21 days after tenancy ends or 15 days after receiving forwarding address, whichever is later

notice.note: nonpay notice runs after the 9-day statutory grace period

deposit_interest_rate.formula: rate set annually by the Banking Commissioner

deposit.note: cap applies to leases of 1 year or more

screening.note: recent legislative activity - verify current status

DC.name: District of Columbia
quirks: Rent Administration Division (RAD) registration required; rent control applies to most pre-1976 buildings with landlords owning 5+ units
Dedicated property-manager license jurisdiction

stabilized_increase.formula: CPI-W + 2%, capped at 10% (elderly/disabled: CPI only, capped at 5%)

deposit.penalty: late claim notice forfeits the right to keep any of the deposit
deposit.interest_owed: only if held in an interest-bearing account (accounting option)
deposit.note: 15 days to return when no claim; 30 days to send an itemized claim notice

screening.note: Miami-Dade ordinance protects source of income; state preemption limits new local rules

GA.name: Georgia

notice.note: nonpayment requires a demand for possession, not a fixed statutory day count; HB 404 added a 3-business-day cure right after filing

quirks: HB 404 (2024) added the 2-month deposit cap and a 3-business-day post-filing cure right

deposit.note: plus 0.5 month allowed as pet deposit
parties may agree to up to 30 days

IL.name: Illinois

deposit.note: itemized statement due in 30 days, return in 45 (applies to 5+ unit buildings); Chicago RLTO is stricter

notice.note: no statewide entry-notice statute; Chicago RLTO requires 48h

quirks: Chicago RLTO replaces much of state law inside the city; Chicago move-in fees commonly used INSTEAD of security deposits to escape RLTO deposit rules
An LLC landlord must appear through an attorney in Cook County eviction court
IL.overlay_note: Chicago is effectively its own regime (RLTO + rental registration)

chicago_deposit_interest_rate.formula: rate set annually by the City Comptroller

deposit.penalty: up to 2 months rent punitive for bad faith

deposit.note: 1 month unfurnished, 1.5 furnished

KY.name: Kentucky

deposit.note: 30-60 days depending on dispute; URLTA applies only in adopting counties

notice.note: 7-day right-to-cure applies in URLTA counties only

quirks: URLTA adopted county-by-county - tenant protections differ sharply between (e.g.) Louisville/Lexington and non-URLTA counties

LA.name: Louisiana

deposit.penalty: $200 or actual damages (whichever greater) for willful noncompliance

notice.note: the 5-day notice is WAIVABLE in the lease and commonly waived

quirks: Civil-law state - landlord-tenant vocabulary and procedure differ from every common-law state; notice waivers are enforceable

deposit.note: 21 days for tenancies at will

notice.note: Portland requires just cause for termination

portland_me_rent_cap.formula: 70% of CPI plus any rent-board actions

MD.name: Maryland

deposit.note: cap dropped to 1 month Oct 2024; interest ~1.5%/yr or statutory index - verify current rate

notice.note: 60-day MTM and 24h entry effective Oct 2025 - verify

MD.overlay_note: Baltimore City requires a rental license to operate

deposit_interest_rate.formula: statutory index (~1.5% or per state schedule)

MA.name: Massachusetts

deposit.note: 5% interest (or bank rate); strict compliance regime - separate escrow account, receipts, statement of condition

late_fee.rule: no fee may be charged until rent is 30 days late

notice.mtm_termination_days: one full rental period (30 days typical)

quirks: The deposit statute is the most dangerous in the country: ANY procedural miss (wrong account, missing receipt, missing condition statement) can void deductions and trigger treble damages + fees - many MA operators simply don't take deposits

deposit_interest_rate.formula: 5% or the actual bank rate, whichever the account yields

screening.note: 2024 law; verify scope (may apply to larger buildings first)

MN.name: Minnesota

deposit.note: 1% simple interest

notice.mtm_termination_days: one rental period plus one day

MN.overlay_note: Minneapolis requires a rental license to operate

st_paul_rent_cap.citation: St. Paul residential rent stabilization ordinance

notice.note: nonpayment requires a rent demand, then suit - no fixed statutory notice period

screening.note: St. Louis and Kansas City ordinances

MT.name: Montana

deposit.note: 10 days when no deductions are taken

quirks: Dedicated property-management license state

deposit.note: plus 0.25 month allowed as pet deposit

NV.name: Nevada

notice.note: 60 days for tenants 60+ or with a disability (on request)

licensing.note: broker license PLUS a property-management permit

quirks: Summary eviction inverts the burden: the TENANT must file an affidavit to contest or the landlord wins by default - one of the fastest processes in the country

NH.name: New Hampshire

deposit.interest_owed: only if held 1 year or more
deposit.note: cap is greater of 1 month or $100

quirks: Good-cause standard applies even to periodic tenancies - no pure no-cause termination

NJ.name: New Jersey

deposit.note: annual interest or credit to tenant

late_fee.rule: 5-business-day grace required for seniors and certain benefit recipients

notice.note: nonpayment suits may be filed without prior notice; habitual-late-payer cases need a notice to cease

quirks: Anti-Eviction Act: virtually no no-cause removals for covered tenancies - the lease effectively renews forever absent good cause
Many municipalities have local rent control
NJ.overlay_note: Municipal rent-control ordinances are common (Newark, Jersey City, etc.)

deposit_interest_rate.formula: money-market / bank rate on the deposit account, credited annually

deposit.interest_owed: required when deposit exceeds 1 month (annual interest)
deposit.note: 1-month cap applies to leases under 1 year

NY.name: New York

late_fee.rule: lesser of $50 or 5% of monthly rent

quirks: NYC is its own regime: rent stabilization, Multiple Dwelling Registration, Good Cause Eviction (2024), housing court backlogs measured in months to years
NY.overlay_note: NYC Multiple Dwelling Registration is license-to-operate; never answer NYC questions from state law alone

rgb_stabilized_renewal.formula: annual 1-yr / 2-yr renewal percentages for rent-stabilized leases

NC.name: North Carolina

deposit.note: 1.5 months MTM, 2 months for longer terms; deposit must sit in a NC trust account or be bonded; 60-day final accounting allowed when damages are still being assessed

quirks: 7-day month-to-month termination notice - the shortest in the nation

deposit.note: pet deposit may add up to $2,500

deposit.penalty: wrongfully withheld amount doubled + attorney's fees
deposit.interest_owed: narrow: 5% on the excess when deposit > $50 or 1 month and held 6+ months

OR.name: Oregon

late_fee.rule: allowed only after a 4-day grace period, with statutory limits

quirks: Statewide rent cap (7% + CPI, buildings 15+ years old)
Dedicated property-management license state
OR.overlay_note: Portland: registration + mandatory relocation assistance on no-cause/rent-increase displacement

statewide_rent_cap.publisher: OR DAS, annually (~Sept for the following year)

PA.name: Pennsylvania

deposit.note: 2 months in year one, 1 month thereafter

notice.note: Philadelphia has its own notice and diversion rules

quirks: Philadelphia: rental license + lead-safe certification + MANDATORY eviction-diversion program before filing
PA.overlay_note: Philadelphia is license-to-operate with a pre-filing diversion mandate

SC.name: South Carolina
quirks: The 5-day nonpay notice can be satisfied ONCE by conspicuous lease language - a compliant lease clause acts as permanent standing notice, allowing immediate filing

deposit.note: itemized accounting due within 45 days on tenant request

TN.name: Tennessee

deposit.note: no hard statutory deadline - 30 days is standard practice; verify per county

quirks: URLTA applies only in counties over ~75k population - rules differ between (e.g.) Nashville/Memphis and rural counties (URLTA counties run closer to tier 2)

deposit.penalty: $100 + 3x wrongfully withheld amount for bad faith
deposit.note: 30-day clock starts at surrender AND receipt of forwarding address

late_fee.rule: capped at 12% of rent (≤4 units) or 10% (larger)

notice.note: the lease can shorten the 3-day nonpay notice to as little as 1 day

UT.name: Utah

deposit.penalty: deposit + $100 if not returned within 5 days of a written demand

late_fee.rule: only as provided in the lease

quirks: 15-day month-to-month termination - among the shortest

deposit.penalty: late return forfeits the right to withhold; willful violation doubles it

late_fee.rule: capped at the greater of $10 or 10% of the periodic rent (or of the amount due, if less)

WA.name: Washington

deposit.note: Seattle caps deposits at 1 month total (deposit + fees)

late_fee.rule: must be reasonable; Seattle caps late fees at $10/mo

quirks: Statewide just-cause regime - no-cause termination is gone for most tenancies
WA.overlay_note: Seattle RRIO registration is license-to-operate; Seattle first-in-time screening and winter-eviction rules

WV.name: West Virginia

deposit.note: 45 days if the unit is re-rented sooner

notice.note: NO pre-filing notice required for nonpayment - the landlord may file immediately

quirks: Zero-notice nonpayment filings - unique nationally

deposit.penalty: 2x as an unfair trade practice (plus fees)

notice.note: 5-day notice carries a right to cure

deposit.note: plus 15 additional days when deductions are itemized

notice.mtm_termination_days: no statute - one rental period by common practice

places.name: San Francisco

places.name: Seattle
